run.runNote: Phase 1 against the mlflow_vuln source tree (MLflow version 2.5.1.dev0 per mlflow/version.py:5), which is the same snapshot the CodeQL database was created from (sha 330bf0b). All file/line evidence below was verified against this checkout.

target.projectDescription: MLflow platform: tracking server (Flask REST API), model registry, project execution engine (MLproject entry points run via subprocess with explicit shells), pyfunc model deployment/serving with environment managers (conda/virtualenv/pip), MLflow AI gateway (FastAPI + gunicorn/uvicorn), and a multi-command click CLI.

evidence: mlflow/ package with ~435 non-test .py files (plus mlflow/R and mlflow/java auxiliary trees)
setup.py + pyproject.toml: setuptools packaging of the 'mlflow' distribution

toolchain.packResolutionExpected: codeql/python-all 7.1.2 resolved from the local pack cache (~/.codeql/packages) by qlpack.yml
toolchain.codeqlExecution: codeql query compile + codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) + codeql bqrs decode --format=csv

scoring.scale: import/package +0.45, route/decorator/annotation +0.30, runtime/bootstrap +0.20, directory/layout +0.05; threshold primary >= 0.75, secondary 0.50-0.74

framework.selected: flask (primary: tracking server + pyfunc scoring server), click (CLI), fastapi (gateway, secondary)
framework.notes: Flask is the primary web framework; the gateway is a FastAPI service started indirectly through a gunicorn subprocess (mlflow/gateway/runner.py). Click is the CLI framework. Source/sink shapes below are derived from repository evidence per references/python.md and references/patterns.md plus the framework shapes for flask/click.

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Externally influenced data enters through (1) the Flask REST API of the tracking/model-registry server (query string, JSON bodies, protobuf-parsed request messages, artifact upload streams), (2) the pyfunc scoring server HTTP surface (JSON/CSV prediction requests, content type), (3) the click CLI (mlflow run/deploy/gateway commands and options), (4) untrusted project/model artifacts: MLproject YAML entry-point commands, MLmodel/conda/python_env YAML loaded by Model.load and environment managers, (5) environment variables (MLFLOW_* settings incl. MLFLOW_CONDA_HOME and MLFLOW_WHEELED_MODEL_PIP_DOWNLOAD_OPTIONS), and (6) general file reads (model artifacts, config files). Command execution concentrates in the project execution engine (bash -c / cmd /c of MLproject commands), the pyfunc/model deployment backends, the container serving entrypoint, the sagemaker deployment path (os.system), and the central _exec_cmd wrapper in mlflow/utils/process.py used by conda/virtualenv/pip environment managers.

sanitizerObservations: mlflow/utils/string_utils.py:130-131 'quote()' = shlex.quote (posix) / mslex_quote (windows) - applied to project parameters in mlflow/projects/_project_spec.py:246 '_sanitize_param_dict' before command.format(); a real shell-quoting barrier for MLproject parameters, though the command template itself and un-quoted segments (e.g. extra_args '--{key} {value}' joined unquoted at _project_spec.py:238) still flow into bash -c at local.py:277
mlflow/server/handlers.py uses 'validate_path_is_safe' / schema assertion helpers on REST request fields - path traversal guards, not shell sanitizers

The pyfunc/conda/virtualenv environment managers pass commands either as argument lists without shell=True (conda env create, pip install) or through explicit ['bash','-c', ...] wrappers; no escaping is applied to the interpolated command strings themselves
inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: Running an MLproject entry point command, building docker images, and creating conda/pip environments is intended MLflow functionality and is NOT automatically treated as a vulnerability; these sites are recorded only as candidate boundaries for labeling (attack requires attacker influence over project/model artifacts, request fields, or environment).

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query compile, then codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) followed by codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware, only genuine resolved calls into external modules
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic module prefix, receiver name, decorator shapes); catches dynamic or unresolved shapes that API graphs miss and is subject to name-collision noise

exclusions: test directories excluded from candidate rows: any path under /tests/ (root tests/ and pylint_plugins/tests/), plus conftest.py fixtures; ~376 test .py files would otherwise dominate every family
examples/ kept (sample project scripts, small count, they document the project-entry-point surface)
logging-only helpers (logger.* / _logger.* / print) are not extracted as candidates; f-strings inside logging calls are excluded from cmd_format rows

uncoveredCases: mlflow/utils/process.py:_exec_cmd forwards **kwargs into subprocess.Popen; dynamic keyword plumbing (e.g. shell=... from virtualenv.py:137) is matched only at the _exec_cmd wrapper level (internal_exec_wrapper), not per-kwarg.

mlflow/server/__init__.py:42-43 registers handlers from the HANDLERS dict in mlflow/server/handlers.py (values are plain function references, keys are protobuf service classes); handler functions are matched via their @catch_mlflow_exception decorator and by flask request.* reads instead of resolving the dict registration.

Protobuf field reads (request_message.filter etc. after parse_dict) are structurally plain attribute reads on a local variable and are not distinguishable from other attribute reads; the _get_request_message call rows (internal_transfer) plus handler-param rows carry the boundary instead.

mlflow/gateway/app.py FastAPI request bodies (pydantic models / Request objects) - the gateway surface is secondary; covered only via json/yaml/env families and the gateway Runner.start sink, not via FastAPI-specific request models.

Bare-name (from-import) subprocess sinks are matched for distinctive names (Popen, check_call, check_output, system, popen, getoutput, getstatusoutput); bare 'run'/'call' are too collision-prone. In this snapshot the from-import forms actually used are Popen (mlflow/models/container, mlflow/models/docker_utils.py, mlflow/sagemaker/__init__.py) and check_call (mlflow/models/container/__init__.py), both covered.
os.execv/spawn* families and commands.getoutput/getstatusoutput are covered by the exec-API table but do not occur in this snapshot's non-test code.
Windows-specific cmd /c and POSIX bash -c branches in mlflow/projects/backend/local.py:277-280 are mutually exclusive at runtime; both are emitted as shell_arg_list candidates.

constraintsHonored.notes: No PyVul vulnerability ground truth was consulted: mlflow_vuln/confirmed_vulns.json, mlflow_vuln/cmd_sinks*.csv and mlflow-db/cmd_sinks.csv / baseline-info.json were deliberately not read. Candidate families are derived from repository evidence and the loaded language/pattern references only. Project source and database were not modified. Only iris/exploration/detection.json, iris/extraction/sources.ql, iris/extraction/sinks.ql (and compiled/run artifacts under iris/extraction plus notes under iris/diagnostics) were written.
